title: Attention-Oriented Execution Conductor: architecture & length-aware kernel selector
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Problem: Our serving runtime picks kernels with a mostly static priority table that doesn’t generalize across new GPU families and bursty conversational seqlen distributions. This causes 95th percentile tail latency spikes and avoidable token-cost regressions when workloads shift (mixed prefill/decode ratios, long-form summaries).

Goal: Build an execution conductor — a pluggable runtime component that recommends per-request kernel candidates using a lightweight feature vector (arch fingerprint, seqlen, token-phase estimate, quantization profile, active batch occupancy) and performs safe online warm-started experimentation to converge on Pareto-efficient kernel choices for latency vs. cost per workload. The conductor should provide reproducible logs and an opt-in canary rollout path via Console.

Scope: design and implement heuristic feature extraction, offline simulator to score kernel candidates using existing microbench corpus, an online lightweight bandit (conservative epsilon + rollback), telemetry schema, and a Console coverage view for kernel-choice regressions. Integration points: runtime kernel registry, prefill/decode scheduler, and rollout APIs used by Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor produces per-request kernel recommendations that reduce median token cost by >= 6% for mixed conversation workloads in A/B against baseline without increasing 95p latency by > 3%
Offline simulator reproduces historical microbenchmarks (correlation R>0.9 with measured cost/latency) for at least 3 GPU families (A100, H100, RTX-8000) using archived traces
Safe exploration mode: online bandit never selects a kernel that violates configured latency SLO for >1% of requests during canary window
Telemetry emitted in runtime with new fields: kernel_suggestion_id, confidence_score, probe_flag, latency_budget, and chosen_kernel_variant
Console shows a per-model kernel-choice drift heatmap and exposes rollback toggle for any live experiment
implementation_steps: Define feature vector schema and lightweight arch fingerprint algorithm (binary-compatible across runtimes)
Extend kernel registry to expose performance priors (microbench stats) with versioned signatures
Build offline simulator that scores kernel combos using historical prefill/decode traces and cost model
Prototype conservative online selector: epsilon-greedy with latency-safety gate and per-customer namespace isolation
Integrate telemetry hooks and add fields to token-level trace events
Create a Console experiment view and canary rollout flow linking to experiment IDs and telemetries
Run staged validation on Dedicated testbeds for three families and perform load tests under mixed seqlen distributions
notes: We intentionally avoid a full RL loop initially — start with bandit-style exploration with explicit safety checks to simplify rollback and reasoning.
Feature vector must stay small (<16 bytes hashed) to minimize runtime path overhead and avoid increased p99 latency.
Quantized model variants present special constraints: smaller kernels often reduce cost but increase decode jitter; treat quantization_profile as a hard constraint in safety checks.
Fallback policy: when confidence_score < threshold OR telemetry missing, use existing static selection to preserve stability.
Plan to reuse existing microbench harness (ENG-314159) for kernel microbench ingestion; need a small adaptor to export to new offline simulator format.
